content.value_statement: LLM teams often lose important context when prompts grow beyond model limits. This skill provides practical strategies for summaries, token budgets, routing, and prompt layout.
actual_capabilities: Explains tiered strategies for full context, summarization, and retrieval routing.
Shows how to place critical instructions at the beginning and end of prompts.
Provides a token budget model for system text, history, query, and response space.
Defines warning checks for missing token counting and naive truncation.
Suggests related skills for retrieval, memory, and prompt caching workflows.
limitations: Does not implement a ready-to-run context management library.
Does not cover embedding models or retrieval system internals.
Requires model-specific token limits and tokenizer behavior from the user environment.
Examples need adaptation before production use.

use_cases.title: Design a chat context policy
use_cases.description: Create rules for keeping recent turns, summarizing older history, and reserving response space.

use_cases.title: Improve long prompt reliability
use_cases.description: Reorder prompts so critical instructions, constraints, and current requests remain prominent.

use_cases.title: Plan context features
use_cases.description: Compare summarization, retrieval, memory, and caching options before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a context strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a long conversation feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the context-window-management skill. Recommend a simple strategy for this chat flow: [describe users, model, average history length, and response needs].

prompt_templates.title: Build a token budget
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design for predictable model calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the context-window-management skill. Allocate a token budget for system instructions, critical context, history, current query, and response for [model and limit].

prompt_templates.title: Review prompt layout
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing prompt.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the context-window-management skill. Review this prompt structure for serial position issues, missing summaries, and lost constraints: [paste outline].

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-tier system
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the context-window-management skill. Design a tiered context system that switches between full history, summarization, retrieval, and memory for [application details].

output_examples.input: A support chat keeps exceeding the model limit after 30 turns.
output_examples.output: The answer recommends counting tokens each turn, keeping the latest messages intact, summarizing older resolved issues, and reserving response capacity.

output_examples.input: A coding assistant forgets project constraints during long sessions.
output_examples.output: The answer suggests moving critical constraints near the system prompt, restating them near the current request, and summarizing older decisions.

output_examples.input: A team needs to choose between summarization and retrieval.
output_examples.output: The answer compares full context, summaries, and retrieval based on token size, information freshness, and relevance requirements.

best_practices: Count tokens before every model request and reserve space for the response.
Preserve user decisions, preferences, and constraints when summarizing old messages.
Place the most important context near the start and the current task near the end.
anti_patterns: Dropping old messages without a summary or decision record.
Using one hardcoded token limit for every model.
Putting critical requirements only in the middle of a long prompt.

faq.question: Does this skill write context management code?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns, examples, and review guidance that users adapt to their own application.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is general and applies to tools that use long prompts or multi-turn context.

faq.question: Does it replace retrieval augmented generation?
faq.answer: No. It explains when retrieval may be useful, but it does not implement retrieval.

faq.question: What inputs are most useful?
faq.answer: Provide the model limit, average history length, required instructions, current prompt structure, and failure examples.

faq.question: Does it prevent all context loss?
faq.answer: No. It reduces risk by prioritizing important information and making truncation explicit.

faq.question: Is token counting still required?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill recommends token counting because character counts do not match model token limits.
